# jev-relevancy

> A search evaluation framework. turbopuffer does retrieval and hosted reranking, Jev (TypeSafe's typed grading model) is the judge, and DuckDB keeps every run, result, grade, and latency and computes the metrics in SQL. It calibrates Jev against Amazon's human-labeled ESCI queries, then runs on your own data without labels. Each study in experiments/ tests one premise with a pass mark written before it ran.

Python 3.12 with uv. Keys go in `.env`: `TURBOPUFFER_API_KEY` for search, `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` for Jev, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` for LLM judges. One CLI, `uv run relevancy`, runs everything: the numbered pipeline steps (`pipeline <step>`), the studies (`list`, `show`, `check`, `base`, `run`, `status`, each with `--json`), and the documented numbers (`evidence`). Steps that cost money only run with `--yes`. Agents should follow the run-study skill, which says to confirm paid steps with a person and to judge results against the pass mark as written.

## Docs

- [README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/README.md): what the framework does, the headline ESCI results, setup, and the numbered pipeline steps.
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/AGENTS.md): how an agent should run, record, or build a study here.
- [.claude/skills/run-study/SKILL.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/.claude/skills/run-study/SKILL.md): the workflow skill: check, confirm cost, run, compare with the pass mark, record the result, build a planned study.
- [experiments/README.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/README.md): the catalog of studies, ranked, with the base every study needs, the rules every study follows, and licences.
- [src/relevancy/cli.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/src/relevancy/cli.py): the `relevancy` CLI. It reads each study's `study.toml`.
- [tests/fakes.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/tests/fakes.py): fake turbopuffer, Jev, and LLM clients and a synthetic warehouse; `uv run pytest` runs every study's steps against them, which shows the scripts run, not that the methods work.
- [experiments/TEMPLATE.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/TEMPLATE.md): the shape of a new study.
- [docs/walkthrough.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/docs/walkthrough.md): every pipeline step, using your own data, rubrics, and the two ways to call Jev.
- [docs/results.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/docs/results.md): the 500-query ESCI run, judge agreement, turbopuffer performance, costs, and how far to trust them.
- [docs/warehouse.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/docs/warehouse.md): the DuckDB tables and SQL recipes.

## Studies

- [judge-wands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-wands/README.md): ready, not yet run. Jev's agreement with human labels holds on Wayfair's catalogue.
- [recall-fusion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/recall-fusion/README.md): ready, not yet run. Relevant products are retrieved but rank below 50; depth and fusion recover them, and the gain survives reranking.
- [relevance-ontology](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-ontology/README.md): ready, not yet run. Matching the query's product category to product categories (both tagged by Jev against the Google taxonomy) improves hybrid search.
- [relevance-attributes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-attributes/README.md): ready, not yet run. A concept stored once per product ('replacement part') fixes the queries that ask for it.
- [relevance-constraints](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-constraints/README.md): ready, not yet run. Checking each query constraint with its own yes/no question closes the Exact/Substitute gap.
- [relevance-reranker-cascade](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-reranker-cascade/README.md): ready, not yet run. Combining rerankers, or escalating only when unsure, matches Voyage for less.
- [judge-trec](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-trec/README.md): ready, not yet run. Jev orders TREC DL systems like NIST's assessors, as well as GPT-4o judges.
- [database-semantic-operators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/database-semantic-operators/README.md): ready, not yet run. Jev makes LLM filters in SQL affordable at table scale.
- [relevance-ltr](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-ltr/README.md): ready, not yet run. A trained ranker beats any single reranker, even trained on Jev's labels.
- [relevance-routing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/relevance-routing/README.md): ready, not yet run. Routing each query type to its own retrieval setting beats the best single setting.
- [recall-rewrites](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/recall-rewrites/README.md): ready, not yet run. Rewrites and document expansion close vocabulary gaps.
- [benchmark-instructions-stark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/benchmark-instructions-stark/README.md): ready, not yet run. Per-condition checks let a cheap model follow multi-condition requests.
- [benchmark-bright](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/benchmark-bright/README.md): ready, not yet run. As a first pass, Jev keeps most of a reasoning reranker's gain for less.
- [judge-batch-order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-batch-order/README.md): done. Product order in a batched Jev request changes the grades.
- [judge-jev-1.14](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-jev-1.14/README.md): done. Jev 1.14.0 judges and reranks better than 1.13.0.
- [judge-negation-audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-negation-audit/README.md): done. On negation queries, when Jev and the human labels disagree, the humans may be the ones who are wrong.
- [judge-truncation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/judge-truncation/README.md): done. Showing the judge 4,000 characters of description instead of 800 changes its agreement with humans.
- [retrieval-followups](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/retrieval-followups/README.md): done. Four small retrieval changes each move quality or latency.
- [turbopuffer-perf](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/experiments/turbopuffer-perf/README.md): done. Know where server time goes, whether results repeat, and what ANN gives up, before tuning retrieval.

## Optional

- [docs/benchmarks.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/docs/benchmarks.md): public benchmarks where Jev could be tested beyond ESCI.
- [NOTICE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/NOTICE): third-party data in the repo and the terms of each dataset the studies download.
- [docs/duckdb-turbopuffer-connector.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rickcrawford/jev-relevancy/main/docs/duckdb-turbopuffer-connector.md): the design that became tpuf-arrow.
- [tpuf-arrow](https://github.com/rickcrawford/tpuf-arrow): the turbopuffer client the scripts use.
